sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: A Hungarian verb changes with the person who does the action. The vocabulary lists show the plain stem: *olvas*, *tanul*, *főz*. To say “I”, add *-ok*, *-ek* or *-ök* to the stem. Choose the ending by the vowels of the stem, as you do for *-ban/-ben*.

sections.title: Which ending?
sections.content: A stem with a back vowel (*a, á, o, u*) takes *-ok*: *olvas* becomes *olvasok*, *tanul* becomes *tanulok*. A stem with a front vowel (*e, é*) takes *-ek*: *beszél* becomes *beszélek*. A stem with *ö* or *ő* takes *-ök*: *főz* becomes *főzök*.
*Ír* has only the vowel *í*, which is neutral, so the vowels cannot choose the ending for you. Learn it as it is: *írok*.
